findings.description: The KMS key does not enable `enable_key_rotation`, so the underlying key material for the audit bucket key is never automatically rotated. A compromised or leaked key retains its validity indefinitely, greatly extending the blast radius for any data protected by this key.

No `policy` is attached to this KMS key, so it falls back to the default key policy that grants the account's root principal full control (kms:*). Combined with the AWS-managed default, this grants broad administrative control over the key and permits any principal later granted IAM permissions to use it, weakening the least-privilege boundary around audit data.

The alias name is derived from `local.env_prefix.value` and is fully predictable (e.g. `alias/<env>-audit-bucket-key`). This is informational only - it discloses environment naming conventions but does not itself grant access, since access is governed by key policy and IAM.
